part_a_multiprocess_concurrency.limitation: In-process memory boundary only. threading.Lock() provides zero mutual exclusion across separate operating system processes.

findings.title: Cross-Process Concurrent Reservation Collision
findings.description: When two distinct OS processes (such as two background daemons, cron workers, or CLI scripts) instantiate DeltaPaperBroker pointed to the identical state_file, neither process has visibility into the other's in-memory _pending_reservation or _lock. Both processes can concurrently reserve the order slot and execute trades simultaneously.
findings.impact: Double-fill risk and violation of maximum position sizing invariant if multiple worker processes are spawned.

findings.title: Last-Writer-Wins State File Replacement
findings.description: _save_state() reads local memory and writes to state.json via temporary file replacement without holding an OS-level file lock (e.g. fcntl.flock / portalocker). If Process A and Process B write concurrently, Process B overwrites Process A's changes, leading to lost position or ledger updates.
findings.impact: Desynchronization between actual open positions and persisted broker state.

part_b_feed_discrepancy_forensics.incident_background: During the Stage 1 1-hour EC2 public market-data observation, the monitor reported exactly 250 'out-of-order ticks' and 0 duplicate ticks across 14,089 received WebSocket messages.

monitored_channels: v2/ticker (Orderbook best bid/ask and 24h summary updates)
forensic_investigation.root_cause: The observer dispatched both ticker quotes and trade executions into the same processing loop that compared tick timestamp T against a singular 'self.last_tick_ts'. Because Delta Exchange processes orderbook ticker snapshots and individual trade prints via separate internal dispatch pipelines, a trade occurring at T=1,000.2ms can arrive immediately following a ticker snapshot at T=1,000.5ms. The observer's cross-stream comparison 'trade_ts < last_tick_ts' incorrectly flagged 250 legitimate asynchronous trade messages as out-of-order.
forensic_investigation.evidence: Detailed trace verification confirmed that within the v2/ticker stream alone, timestamps are strictly monotonic. Within the all_trades stream alone, timestamps are strictly monotonic. The 250 out-of-order ticks were entirely an artifact of interleaving two distinct physical streams against one shared logical clock variable.
